welcome.introReturning: Pick up where you left off, or start a new flow from a template.
welcome.step1Body: Working flows you can copy in one click — Excel → DB, webhook → Slack, daily reports. Easiest way to poke around and see what's possible.
welcome.step2Body: Drop a few steps on a blank canvas and wire them up. Slack, Gmail, Sheets, Postgres — they're all in the catalog.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.subtitle: Let members sign in with your identity provider instead of a password.
sso.googleIntro: Create an OAuth 2.0 client in your Google Cloud project, set the redirect URI below, then paste the client ID and secret here.
sso.walkthroughSummary: First time? How to create the Google OAuth client (4 steps)
sso.walkthroughIntro: You'll do this once, in Google Cloud Console. It usually takes 3–5 minutes. Keep this tab open — you'll come back to paste two values.
sso.walkthroughStep1Body: Go to <0>console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials</0> and sign in with a Google Workspace admin account. Pick the project for your company, or create a new one (top bar → project picker → "New project").
sso.walkthroughStep2Body: In the left sidebar, click "OAuth consent screen". Choose <0>Internal</0> if your team uses Google Workspace (recommended — only people in your domain can sign in). Fill in an app name (e.g. "Hazyflow") and a support email, then Save and continue through the remaining screens. You can skip the Scopes step.
sso.walkthroughStep3Body: Back under "Credentials", click <0>+ Create credentials → OAuth client ID</0>. For "Application type" pick <1>Web application</1>. Name it "Hazyflow". Under "Authorized redirect URIs", click "+ Add URI" and paste this exact URL — use the Copy button below; even one wrong character (a trailing slash, a missed letter) means Google will reject sign-in:
sso.walkthroughStep4Head: Copy the Client ID and secret
sso.walkthroughStep4Body: Click <0>Create</0>. Google shows a popup with your <1>Client ID</1> and <1>Client secret</1>. Copy both — the secret is only shown once. Paste them into the form below and click Save.
sso.walkthroughTip: Tip: if you don't see "Internal" as an option, your account isn't a Workspace admin. Ask whoever administers your company's Google accounts to either do this step or grant you admin on the Cloud project.
sso.redirectUriDesc: Add this exact URL under "Authorized redirect URIs" on the Google OAuth client.
sso.redirectUriUnavailable: Set the server's public base URL to see the exact redirect URI to paste into Google.
sso.clientIdDesc: From the Google OAuth client — looks like 1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com.
sso.clientSecretDesc: From the Google OAuth client. Stored encrypted; not shown again after saving.
sso.clientSecretStored: A secret is stored. Leave blank to keep it; paste a new one to replace it.
sso.workspaceDomainDesc: If set, only Google accounts in this domain (e.g. acme.com) can sign in. Leave blank to allow any Google account whose email matches a member.
sso.disableConfirm: Disable Google sign-in for this organization? Members who relied on it will need to use password sign-in.
sso.activeHead: Members can now sign in with Google
sso.activeBody: Share this URL with your team: <0>{{signinUrl}}</0>. The Google button appears on the sign-in page for anyone who opens that link.
sso.testButtonDesc: Opens Google sign-in in a new tab using your own Google account. If Google accepts your credentials, you'll come back here with a confirmation — and you'll know your team can sign in too.
sso.popupBlockedHead: Your browser blocked the test popup
sso.popupBlockedBody: Either allow popups for this site and click Test sign-in again, or
sso.popupBlockedTail: (you'll leave this page and come back when Google's done).
sso.testSuccessBody: Google accepted your Client ID and secret, and the redirect URI matches. Your team can now sign in at the link above.
sso.testErrorRetry: Fix the issue above, click Save again, then click Test sign-in to try once more.

testError.invalid_client: Google didn't recognize your Client ID or secret. This usually means a typo (the secret is only shown once in Google's popup, so it's easy to miss the last character). Re-paste both values and click Save again.
testError.redirect_uri_mismatch: Google says the redirect URI doesn't match what's on your OAuth client. Copy the redirect URI shown above and paste it under "Authorized redirect URIs" in Google — it has to match exactly, with no trailing slash or extra spaces.
testError.invalid_grant: Google rejected the sign-in code. This usually means the test took too long. Click Test sign-in again — it should work on the second try.
testError.unauthorized_client: Google says this OAuth client isn't authorized to sign users in. The most common cause is picking the wrong client type — make sure you created a "Web application" client, not "Desktop" or "Service account".
testError.exchange_failed: Google rejected the credentials when we tried to verify them. Re-paste the Client ID and secret carefully, then Save and try again.
testError.no_email: Google didn't return an email address. This shouldn't happen for normal Workspace accounts — if it keeps happening, the OAuth consent screen may be missing the email or profile scope.
testError.not_verified: The Google account you signed in with doesn't have a verified email. Try signing in with a different Workspace account.
testError.domain_mismatch: You signed in with a Google account that isn't in your Workspace domain — that's what the domain restriction is supposed to do, so this is actually a sign it's working. To verify the full flow, click Test sign-in again and pick an account in your Workspace.
testError.not_configured: The Google sign-in settings were changed while the test was running. Refresh the page and try again.
testError.denied: The sign-in was cancelled or blocked before completing. If you clicked "Cancel" in Google's chooser, click Test sign-in again and pick an account. If Google blocked it, your Workspace admin may have a policy that needs adjusting.
testError.internal: Hazyflow couldn't finish the sign-in on its end. This isn't a problem with your Google config — it's most likely a temporary backend issue. Try again in a minute, or check the daemon logs if it keeps failing.

issueKey.title: Issue API key

issueKey.templateOperatorDesc: Run and edit flows. Read secrets.

editor.triggersTitle: Configure how this flow starts — form, webhook, or schedule

editor.emptyBody: Add your first step to get started — pick an app like ntfy or Slack, or a building block.
editor.emptyEntryBody: Every flow starts with an entry point that decides when it runs — a Schedule, a Webhook, or an Interval. Add one, then build the steps that follow.
editor.pauseTitle: Pause this flow — stops scheduled, interval and webhook runs. Manual Run still works.
editor.resumeTitle: This flow is paused — click to resume automatic runs.
editor.pauseSaveFirst: Save the flow before pausing it.
editor.triggerHint: This flow only runs when you press Run. Add a trigger to start it automatically — on a schedule, from a form, or a webhook.
editor.configBlock: Can't run yet — “{{label}}” needs setup: {{detail}}. Fill it in, then run.
editor.runFailedNoDetail: open the step to see details
editor.addFrameTitle: Add a comment frame to group steps
editor.groupSubgraphTitle: Collapse the selected steps into a subgraph
editor.configWarnTitle: Steps are missing required values — set them before running
editor.configModalLead_one: 1 step still needs required values before this flow can run. Select it to jump to it on the canvas.
editor.configModalLead_other: {{count}} steps still need required values before this flow can run. Select one to jump to it on the canvas.
editor.breakpointTitle: Toggle a breakpoint — the run pauses after this step so you can inspect its output
editor.continueTitle: Resume the run until the next breakpoint or the end
editor.stepTitle: Run the next step, then pause again
editor.publishedTitle: The current release — the version automatic triggers run (when the flow is live).
editor.publishChangesTitle: Publish your draft — automatic triggers will run these changes.
editor.publishFirstTitle: Go live — publishes this flow and starts its automatic triggers.

editor.confirmPauseBody: All automatic triggers stop firing — cron, poll, webhook, and forms. Manual Run still works, and the live version is kept so resuming restores it.
editor.confirmUpdateBody: The live version updates to your current draft. Automatic triggers will run the new version from now on.
editor.diffTitle: See what changed since the published version
editor.diffNone: The draft matches the published version.
editor.makeLiveTitle: Publish this version — automatic triggers will run it (rollback).
editor.label: Label
editor.labelTitle: Name this version (e.g. "Black Friday config") so it's easy to find later.
editor.labelHint: Leave blank to clear the label. The name stays attached to this version across publishes and rollbacks.
editor.confirmMakeLiveBody: This rolls the live version back to this revision — automatic triggers will run it from now on. Give it a name so it's easy to recognise later.
editor.testRunHelp: Edit the JSON payload below, then fire it through this flow's webhook trigger. The run uses your current draft.
editor.runTestTrigger: Runs once now, to test. To run automatically on new responses, click Publish.
editor.testEventTooltip: Fire this flow with a sample submission to check it works end-to-end
editor.connNeededAskAdmin: Ask an org admin to connect these.
